messages:
Eileen (AM): opening MeridianBank POC thread. They need Redwood Private in their AWS account, must complete security questionnaire, and require a single static egress IP for allowlisting. POC window: 10 business days.
Jon (SE): two main asks from Meridian: 1) preserve original client source IP to their downstream services, 2) secure control-plane comms (mTLS preferred). They asked if PrivateLink or VPC Peering is better.
Priya (NetOps): PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoints) is usually the least friction: stable DNS names, no route-table changes, works cross-account without CIDR peering. VPC Peering is ok but breaks with overlapping CIDRs and needs careful route management.
Sam (Solutions Eng): recommended deployment options (short):
- Quick POC (low cost): deploy Redwood Private in their VPC but reuse their existing NAT -> outbound SNAT -> provides connectivity quickly but loses client IP.
- Allowlist-capable POC (higher infra cost): provision NAT Gateway(s) with EIPs per AZ for stable outbound IPs, OR use NLBs with EIPs and proxy-protocol v2 to preserve client IP when running in-customer.
Priya (NetOps): sample PrivateLink validation: run curl against the interface endpoint FQDN and pass Host header for virtual hosts.
Sam (Solutions Eng): example test command:
```
curl -v https://vpce-0a1b2c3d.vpce-svc-xyz.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com/health -H 'Host: api.redwood-inference.com'
```
Lena (InfoSec): questionnaire wording suggestion: "No public inbound ports required. Outbound HTTPS (443) only to control-plane FQDNs (*.redwood-inference.com). TLS v1.2+ enforced. Customers may require static egress IPs; we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. Key usage is logged in CloudTrail."
Eileen (AM): pricing/ops question: will EIPs/NAT gateways drive POC costs materially? Need to advise Meridian.
Sam (Solutions Eng): yes; NAT Gateways + EIPs have hourly/GB charges. Offer two patterns on the quote: Minimal (reuse NAT, minimal infra cost) vs Isolated (dedicated NAT Gateways + EIPs per AZ, higher infra cost). Provide ballpark daily estimate in the quote.
Priya (NetOps): additional note: if Meridian uses corporate TLS inspection/proxy, SNI rewrite will break TLS to our endpoints. Recommend either a bypass for our endpoint hostnames or mTLS to avoid MITM.
Jon (SE): for firewall rules to include in questionnaire: outbound 443 to: 1) control plane FQDNs (*.redwood-inference.com), 2) model store (s3.amazonaws.com or our model-registry fqdn), 3) optional telemetry endpoints. Prefer FQDN allowlist; if IPs required, provide EIP list from customer's NAT/EIPs.
Lena (InfoSec): I'll draft the attestation snippet and include links to SOC2.pdf and ISO27001.pdf. ETA next business day.
Eileen (AM): action items: Sam -> one-page network diagram + curl test (ETA today). Priya -> firewall + NAT/EIP pattern + short runbook (ETA EOD). Lena -> questionnaire attestation and cert links (ETA tomorrow). Jon -> KMS/legal blurbs.
deploy-bot: sandbox for Meridian POC provisioned in us-west-2 (build-1204). :rocket:
Priya (NetOps): final caveat: avoid VPC Peering if they have multi-spoke transit with overlapping ranges; Transit Gateway or PrivateLink are safer.
Eileen (AM): thanks team, will collate and send to Meridian security team. Add tiny clarifications inline if needed.
Jon (SE): one-liner to add to questionnaire: "Control plane and model artifacts served over TLS 1.2+ to public FQDNs; customers can guarantee egress with dedicated EIPs for allowlisting."
Lena (InfoSec): and: "Private deployments support customer-managed CMKs; all KMS calls are recorded in CloudTrail for audit."
Eileen (AM): closing loop - I'll attach the diagram and runbook to the questionnaire."
